open_issues: The real steps keep the Steps defaults (Unchanged, checks pass, cap 0), so the rule and the share run only in tests. The A6 wiring (Steps::rebase, Athena::rebase_for_landing) is absent, as the plan expected. The share is not yet measured in a live drain. The CHANGELOG, the design doc and the drain.rs module docs say so.
Rebase conflict handling (hold the job, no retry, no drain stop), the thrash stop and the send-back were not built. They belong to A6 and are out of scope.

The plan's open questions about the rule stay open. I followed the plan: every Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock at any depth forces a re-check, only moved rebases count in the share, and a re-check that fails twice ends as repeated-failure. Each is a small edit to change.

The unit tests for rebase_needs_recheck sit in the `read_ahead_tests` module in drain.rs, because that module has the `own` helper. The plan's filter `drain::tests::rebase` does not match them; use `cargo test -p athena-cli --lib rebase_needs`.

The drain-level tests are in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs rather than src/drain.rs, as the plan and expected deliverables say. Criterion 1's wording names src/drain.rs, so the verifier may want to know.
mistakes: None found. All new tests passed on the first run.
learnings: The landing queue and Rebase handling (LandingQueue; plan_rebase and rebase_job_branch in landing.rs) are in the tree, but drain.rs never calls them. Steps::rebase and Athena::rebase_for_landing do not exist, so the rule cannot run in a live drain yet.

Drain::land is called again after NotLanded with the same `passed` slot, and the job is not re-run. This is why a failed re-check must be remembered (the `owing` set): a second `rebase` finds the branch already moved and answers Unchanged.
pass_over lines go to the Ui, not to Report. A test must use a recording Ui (`Lines` in tests/common) to assert them.
display::drain already prints report.notes, so the share line needed no display.rs change.
desires: A way to run only the new tests by a stable filter name; the plan's `drain::tests::rebase` filter does not match because the unit tests sit in the read_ahead_tests module, so I used `rebase_needs`.
